Project Setup: Nuxt 3 projects are created using the nuxi CLI. The scaffolding tool asks about desired features like package manager, UI framework, and modules, generating a ready-to-develop project structure.

npx nuxi init my-app
cd my-app
npm install
npm run dev
Pages: The pages directory in Nuxt automatically generates routes based on file structure. Each .vue file becomes a route, with index.vue as the root and dynamic routes using brackets like [id].vue.
Routing: Nuxt provides <NuxtLink> for client-side navigation and <NuxtPage> for rendering matched routes. Route middleware can be defined to protect pages or redirect users based on conditions.

useFetch: useFetch is the simplest way to fetch data in Nuxt 3. It automatically deduplicates requests, handles caching, and provides reactive refs for data, pending state, and error handling.
useAsyncData: useAsyncData provides more control over data fetching than useFetch. It accepts a custom fetcher function and supports keys for caching, refresh intervals, and lazy loading options.
Server Routes: Server routes in the server/api directory handle backend logic with h3 event handlers. They support all HTTP methods and can access request body, query parameters, and cookies directly.

Universal: Universal rendering is Nuxt's default mode, combining server-side rendering with client-side hydration. The server renders HTML on first request, then Vue takes over for SPA-like navigation.

// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({ ssr: true })
SPA: Single Page Application mode disables server-side rendering entirely. All rendering happens client-side, with the server only serving a minimal HTML shell. Useful for fully client-driven apps.

// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({ ssr: false })
Static Generation: Static generation pre-renders all pages at build time using nuxt generate. The output is a fully static site deployable on any static hosting provider like Netlify or Vercel.

Auth: The @sidebase/nuxt-auth module provides a complete authentication system for Nuxt 3. It supports multiple auth providers, session management, and middleware protection out of the box.
Content: Nuxt Content is a file-based CMS that reads Markdown, JSON, and YAML files from the content directory. It provides a queryable MongoDB-like API and automatic rendering of content files.

// content/index.md
---
title: Hello Nuxt
---
# Welcome
<script setup>
const { data } = await useAsyncData('content', () => queryContent('/').find());
</script>
Tailwind: The Nuxt Tailwind module integrates Tailwind CSS with zero configuration. It auto-imports the config, enables HMR for styles, and purges unused classes in production builds.
SEO: Nuxt provides built-in SEO tools through useHead composable and the @nuxtjs/seo module. It manages meta tags, Open Graph, structured data, and sitemaps for better search visibility.

useState: useState is Nuxt's built-in reactive state composable that works across server and client. It creates a singleton ref that persists across component re-renders and is serialized during SSR.

const counter = useState('counter', () => 0);
const increment = () => counter.value++;
Pinia: Pinia is the recommended state management library for Nuxt 3. It provides a intuitive API with full TypeScript support, devtools integration, and automatic SSR hydration.
Store Patterns: Nuxt stores follow the composition API pattern with defineStore. Stores can be organized by domain feature and accessed anywhere in the app via the generated composable function.

Route Middleware: Route middleware in Nuxt runs before entering a route and can redirect or cancel navigation. Middleware files are placed in the middleware directory and can be applied globally or per-route.
Auth Module: The nuxt-auth module provides session-based authentication with built-in login pages, OAuth support, and credential-based auth. It automatically handles token refresh and session persistence.

const { status, signIn, signOut, data } = useAuth();
if (status.value === 'unauthenticated') signIn('github');

Vercel: Deploying Nuxt to Vercel requires the Vercel preset. Vercel automatically detects the framework, optimizes serverless functions, and provides edge network distribution.

// nuxt.config.ts
export default defineNuxtConfig({ nitro: { preset: 'vercel' } });
Netlify: Nuxt deploys to Netlify using the Netlify preset, generating edge functions for server routes. Netlify provides automatic HTTPS, deploy previews, and form handling.
Node Server: The Node server preset runs Nuxt as a standalone Node.js application. This is ideal for self-hosting on VPS, Docker containers, or traditional server environments.

Auto-imports: Nuxt automatically imports composables, components, and utilities from predefined directories. Components in components/, composables in composables/, and utils in utils/ are auto-imported without explicit imports.
Layers: Nuxt layers allow extending a base Nuxt project from external sources or local directories. Layers can override components, pages, composables, and configuration, enabling modular architectures.
Modules Dev: Creating custom Nuxt modules allows packaging reusable functionality. Modules can modify the Nuxt configuration, add hooks, register components, and integrate with the build pipeline.
